# Results — Study 597 (Guyton-Klinger Guardrails)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Guyton 2004; Guyton & Klinger 2006) — **dynamic withdrawals with guardrails (freeze the
inflation raise after a losing year, cut 10% above an upper guardrail, raise 10% below a lower
one) let a retiree safely START at 5%+ where the fixed 4% rule is the ceiling** — tested on
30-year retirement cohorts on the Shiller 1871+ tape. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-07-03** (run date); the
cached Shiller extract's last **complete full-data month is 2023-06** — no partial months are
used. Fingerprint `b0b11b1f3080`. Cousin of studies [173](../../173-four-percent-rule/) (the
FIXED 4% rule, Real) and [596](../../596-bond-tent-glidepath/) (glidepath shape, same cohort
framework); what is new here is the **DYNAMIC withdrawal policy** — the rules act on the
withdrawal, not the allocation.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | Shiller S&P 500 monthly (GitHub raw mirror, cache-first `_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`) |
| Window | 1871-02 → 2023-06 (**1,829 months**); nominal EQ total return **+9.16%/yr**, nominal BD **+4.56%/yr** (10-year first-order approx), CPI **+2.12%/yr** |
| Simulation space | **Nominal** (the GK rules are defined on nominal amounts and nominal withdrawal rates); every income/wealth outcome deflated by realised CPI back to **real** — algebraically the Bengen case matches sibling 596's real-space simulator (fixed-4% success **96.26%** here vs 96.33% there; the residual is a second-order compounding convention, stated not hidden) |
| Cohorts | **1,470** monthly-start 30-year retirements (1871-02 → 1993-07), withdrawal at the start of each year, annual rebalance to 60/40 |
| Rules (GK 2006) | inflation raise = last year's CPI capped at +6%, **frozen** when last year's portfolio return was negative and current WR > initial; **cut −10%** when current WR > 1.2× initial (only while >15 years remain); **raise +10%** when current WR < 0.8× initial |
| Execution / costs | one clean lag: every rule input (last year's inflation, last year's return, current portfolio value) is known at the start-of-year withdrawal date; **10 bps one-way × traded value** (withdrawal sales + rebalance turnover) |
| Machinery identity | guardrails at (0, ∞) with no freeze/cap ≡ Bengen: max \|income-path difference\| = **0.0** (exact) |

> **No survivorship:** the tape is a single index series, not a survivor panel. The named bias
> is the opposite one: the US is the **best-performing equity market in recorded history**,
> which flatters every rule that keeps the retiree invested — and both rules here get it.

## Success rates — the mechanical rescue is total

Share of the 1,470 cohorts never depleted over 30 years:

| initial rate | fixed (Bengen) | **GK guardrails** |
|---|--:|--:|
| 4.0% | 96.26% | **100.00%** |
| 4.5% | 88.50% | **100.00%** |
| 5.0% | **75.65%** | **100.00%** |
| 5.5% | 63.27% | **100.00%** |
| 6.0% | 53.88% | 99.80% |

SAFEMAX (highest initial rate surviving *every* cohort): fixed **3.68%** · guardrails
**5.83%**. At a 5% start the fixed rule ruins **24.35%** of retirements; the guardrails ruin
**none** (bootstrap 95% CI on the Δsuccess: **[+0.75, +48.17] pp** — wide because ruin lives in
a few decades, but excludes 0).

## Headline strategies — all quantities real, initial wealth = 1

| strategy | success | LTI mean/median/p05 | min-income median/p05/worst | cuts | raises | freezes |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| fixed 4% | 96.26% | 1.195 / 1.200 / 1.200 | 0.0400 / 0.0400 / 0.0000 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| fixed 5% | 75.65% | 1.422 / 1.500 / 0.994 | 0.0500 / 0.0000 / 0.0000 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **GK 5%** | **100.00%** | **1.633 / 1.508 / 0.988** | **0.0374 / 0.0205 / 0.0169** | 1.1 | 4.8 | 4.5 |
| GK 5.5% | 100.00% | 1.697 / 1.569 / 1.023 | 0.0391 / 0.0206 / 0.0167 | 1.3 | 4.0 | 4.9 |

*LTI = 30-year lifetime real income per $1 of initial portfolio; min-income = the worst
single-year real paycheck; cuts/raises/freezes = mean rule events per 30-year cohort.*

## Inference — HAC *t* (Newey-West, bandwidth = full 360-month overlap) + bootstrap

Block-bootstrap 95% CIs: 1,000 reps, circular 120-month blocks on the joint EQ/BD/CPI monthly
tape, seed 597 (blocks preserve within-decade dynamics, destroy cross-decade mean reversion —
stated, not hidden).

| comparison | mean Δ | HAC *t* | bootstrap 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **LTI GK 5% − fixed 4%** (the claimed raise) | **+0.437** | **+4.23** | [+0.128, +0.970] |
| LTI GK 5.5% − fixed 4% | +0.501 | +4.70 | — |
| LTI GK 5% − fixed 5% | +0.211 | +2.23 | [−0.054, +0.709] |
| TW GK 5% − fixed 5% (terminal wealth) | −0.115 | −0.60 | [−1.399, +0.211] |
| Δsuccess @5% (GK − fixed) | **+24.35 pp** | — (rate) | [+0.745, +48.167] |

Reading: the headline claim clears the bar. Starting at 5% with guardrails paid **more
lifetime real income than the 4% rule** (+0.44 per $1 initial, HAC *t* = **+4.23**, bootstrap
CI excludes 0) while ruining **zero** of 1,470 cohorts (fixed 5%: 358 ruins). The mechanism is
arithmetic — withdrawals that shrink when the portfolio shrinks cannot easily deplete it — and
the tape shows the number with certified uncertainty.

## The price — ruin risk is converted into paycheck risk, not removed

- GK 5% spends a **mean 6.92 years** (median 4, max 25) below the 4%-rule paycheck;
  **54.69%** of cohorts dip below it at least once (GK 5.5%: mean 6.41 years, 51.77%).
- **22.86%** of cohorts end 30 years with **less** lifetime real income from GK 5% than from
  the plain 4% rule.
- Worst-cohort paycheck floor: **0.0169** — a **66% real cut** from the initial 0.050. The
  fixed rule never cuts; it ruins instead (min-income p05 at 5% is 0.0000).
- Famous cohorts (lifetime real income per $1): retire **1929-09** — fixed4 1.200 (ok),
  fixed5 1.172 (**ruin**), GK5 **0.988** (ok, min paycheck 0.0241, 7 cuts + 7 freezes); retire
  **1966-01** — fixed4 1.029 (ruin), fixed5 0.910 (ruin), GK5 **0.870** (ok, min paycheck
  0.0189); retire **1972-12** — fixed4 1.200 (ok), GK5 1.076 (ok). In the two worst regimes the
  "successful" guardrails plan paid **less total income than the failing fixed rules** — it
  survives *by* paying you less, exactly when you are poorest.

## Which rule does the rescue? (variants at a 5% start)

| variant | success | LTI mean | min-inc median / worst | cuts | raises | freezes |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| GK (full 2006) | 100.00% | 1.633 | 0.0374 / 0.0169 | 1.1 | 4.8 | 4.5 |
| freeze-only (no guardrails) | 97.41% | 1.314 | 0.0376 / 0.0000 | 0 | 0 | 3.2 |
| no prosperity raise | 100.00% | 1.250 | 0.0363 / 0.0169 | 0.9 | 0 | 2.6 |
| capital-preservation always (no 15-yr limit) | 100.00% | 1.600 | 0.0355 / 0.0152 | 2.2 | 5.3 | 4.3 |

The **capital-preservation cut is the rescue** (freeze alone still ruins 2.59%); the
**prosperity raise is the income** (+0.38 LTI vs no-raise). Both halves are needed for the
headline.

## Robustness — allocation × costs

GK 5% success is **100.00%** and LTI mean 1.630–1.680 at every combination of 60/40 vs 65/35
(the GK paper's allocation) and 0 / 10 / 25 bps one-way costs; fixed 5% success stays 75.6–77.4%.
Costs are a non-factor (a retiree trades a few % of NAV per year).

## Synthetic control — the engine is faithful

20 independent seeded worlds per setting; detector = Δsuccess (GK − fixed, same rate),
one-sample *t* across worlds. *(Machinery proof only — never cited as market evidence.)*

| world | fixed-rule failures | Δsuccess (pp) | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **EXACT NULL** — calm world (vol 10%, wr 3%): nothing to rescue | 0.00% | **+0.00 in every seed** | n/a (all-zero) |
| mild ruin (vol 10%, wr 4%) | 2.84% | +2.84 | +4.51 |
| **PLANTED** — historical vol (17%), wr 5% | 35.09% | **+34.27** | **+16.90** |
| PLANTED — high vol (25%), wr 5% | 47.57% | +38.39 | +24.24 |
| PLANTED — historical vol (17%), wr 6% | 59.21% | +50.76 | +28.37 |

The detector reads exactly zero where no fixed-rate ruin exists and lights up in proportion to
the ruin planted — so the real-tape rescue is not a construction artefact. (The +0.18 ΔLTI in
the calm world is the prosperity rule mechanically paying raises — expected, and stated.)

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The claim is mechanically true on 152 years of US tape and the tape
  certifies it: at a 5% start the guardrails survive **all 1,470** cohorts where the fixed rule
  ruins **24.35%** (bootstrap CI excludes 0), guardrails SAFEMAX **5.83%** vs fixed **3.68%**,
  and lifetime real income beats the 4% rule by **+0.44 per $1** (HAC *t* = **+4.23**, CI
  [+0.13, +0.97]). Robust to allocation (60/40, 65/35) and costs (0–25 bps). No survivorship
  (single index series); named caveat: the US is history's best equity market and flatters both
  rules.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Trivially implementable (two ETFs, one rule check per year, costs
  immaterial) with unlimited capacity — but what you deploy is **not a safe 5% paycheck**. The
  income is regime-dependent by construction: 55% of cohorts spend years (mean ~7) below the
  4%-rule paycheck, the worst floor is a **66% real cut**, and 23% of cohorts end with less
  lifetime income than the plain 4% rule. "100% success" is earned by redefining success as
  "never hits zero", not "keeps paying you".
- **Third axis — "Is the 5%+ start a free lunch?" — BUSTED.** Ruin risk is **converted into
  paycheck risk, not removed**. In 1929 and 1966 — the exact regimes the pitch invokes — the
  guardrails plan paid *less* lifetime income (0.988 and 0.870) than the fixed rules that
  "failed" (1.200 and 1.029): it survives by cutting your income when you are poorest. The
  guardrails are an insurance policy whose premium is deducted from the paycheck; a retiree
  with rigid spending needs cannot actually collect the advertised 5%.
